name: Classic
summary: Familiar and always visible: a docked app bar on the left, full title bars and your desktop icons.
description: A familiar desktop: a dock that is always visible along the left edge and reserves its space, a top bar showing workspaces and the focused application, minimize and maximize buttons on every window, and desktop icons kept. No hot corner, so nothing happens by surprise.

settings.reason: Original JERONIX icons; anything JERONIX does not draw falls back to Yaru and Adwaita.
Older (GTK 3) applications use the sage variant instead of Ubuntu orange.
A neutral interface typeface instead of Ubuntu's own.
Documents use the same neutral typeface.
JERONIX's primary dark look.
Ubuntu shows the slate accent as Yaru sage, the JERONIX secondary color, instead of Ubuntu orange.
Nothing opens unless you ask for it.
Weekday next to the time.
Familiar title bar buttons.
Double-click a title bar to maximize, as on most desktops.
Workspaces appear as needed.
Drag-to-edge tiling.
New windows open in the middle of the screen.
JERONIX light wallpaper.
JERONIX dark wallpaper.
Fill the screen without distortion.
The JERONIX menu is labeled, like a start menu.
Workspaces are always visible in the top bar.
The focused application and its windows menu are always visible.
The JERONIX menu replaces Activities.
A vertical app bar on the left.
Always visible; windows maximize next to it, never under it.
Compact icons for a persistent bar.
Running applications appear after favorites.
Window previews on hover.

limitations: Desktop icons (ding) are left as they are.
The dock lives on the primary monitor only.
